topics.label: Río Andarax restoration works (2023 procurement)
topics.description: A proposed hydrological and ecological restoration works contract for the Río Andarax, covering Alhabia, Santa Fe de Mondújar, Gádor, Rioja and Benahadux. The June 2023 justification combines flood-risk reduction for neighbouring agricultural land with recovery of native river habitats and natural/ethnographic heritage. Measures include restoring conveyance, native vegetation and traditional balates, transverse structures and boqueras, with interpretive access. The document gives an 18-month execution period, a 106.5 ha project scope and a tender budget of EUR 3,416,081.25 including VAT. The October document evaluates bidders’ technical submissions; neither source certifies completed works or ecological outcomes.

topics.description: The Andarax justification places its proposed works within Spain’s PRTR Component 4, Investment 3, ecosystem restoration and green infrastructure. Its stated 100% financing concerns that public contract; it is not an aid rate available to another applicant. The document ties delivery to reporting on hectares and expenditure, audit traceability, DNSH, antifraud/conflict-of-interest controls and communication. topics.label: Andarax technical tender scoring
topics.description: The 17 October 2023 technical commission report evaluates 25 admitted bidders. Compliance ratings award 0%, 50% or 100% of each subcriterion’s allocated points. Its table groups 21 points for the technical report/project understanding, 9 for work programme/materials and 15 for environmental-impact study, giving 45 possible technical points. The highest listed technical result is 40.5, for Construcciones Porman, SA. These are procurement technical scores; the report does not establish the final contract award or a LEADER selection score. The full underlying PCAP subcriterion definitions are referenced but not contained here.

topics.label: Holm oak (Q. rotundifolia source concept)
topics.description: Quercus rotundifolia is an evergreen Mediterranean oak described in the Umbría de la Virgen sheet as a tree up to 20 m, sometimes shrubby, with leathery leaves and grey felted undersides. It forms dense or open sclerophyll woodland on varied substrates; the stated altitude range is 0–1700 (2000) m. The sheet reports occurrence across all Andalusian provinces, becoming scarcer in low southeastern areas, and adaptation to summer drought and inland weather extremes. Its habitat overview explicitly excepts the most arid zones: drought tolerance does not establish suitability for every semiarid restoration site or a seedling watering dose. This source concept remains separate from the handbook’s Q. ilex identity; existing illustration metadata and community links are retained.
topics.name_note: The factsheet Quercus rotundifolia source concept remains separate from the handbook Quercus ilex concept, despite their shared common names.

topics.label: Doñana agricultural and forest restoration grants (2025)
topics.description: The library’s 13 October 2026 proposal concerns a 2025 Fundación Biodiversidad competition for agrarian/forest renaturalisation and ecological restoration in Doñana’s area of influence. It proposes beneficiaries, reserves and unsuccessful evaluated applications. The proposal is provisional and expressly creates no beneficiary right before the award resolution is notified or published. Its geography is specific to Doñana; it does not establish an Almería funding route. A total score of 50 alone is insufficient: the source also requires 25 points in each technical and strategic block. Current call and award status remain unverified.

topics.label: Groasis Growboxx biodegradable reservoir
topics.description: A supplier-described recycled-paper planting reservoir with a central tree opening and four additional seed pockets. Unlike Groasis Waterboxx, this datasheet specifies no wick: its capillary bottom mediates water release according to soil conditions. The cover has a rain-collecting siphon that also permits refilling. The vendor describes approximately half-year onset of decomposition, a box degrading within a year and a cover lasting five years; these are product claims rather than independently verified Almería outcomes. The sheet does not give a checked storage capacity or a drone docking/interface specification. Its daily release range is not a species-specific event dose. Groasis uses the marketing term plant cocoon; this does not identify the separate Cocoon product already in the graph.

topics.label: Groasis Waterboxx reusable reservoir (Twinboxx)
topics.description: A supplier-described polypropylene reservoir with a twin central opening, rain/dew collection and a nylon wick. The version-2 datasheet gives approximately 15 L content, 1.4 kg mass and 50 × 22 cm diameter/height. A capped cover opening permits refilling. The vendor describes reuse across planting cycles, removal after roots establish (roughly 6–18 months in its narrative) and wick cleaning/replacement. Stated daily supply varies from 700 to 18 mL, averaging about 50 mL depending on soil; this is not an event dose for carob or either of the possible two plants. Performance and biomass claims are vendor statements with a customer-validation disclaimer. The document’s validity date is 31 December 2023, not a verified publication date or proof of present availability.

topics.label: Small-reservoir refill access
topics.description: Refill access is the opening and servicing arrangement used to add water to a local planting reservoir. The reviewed Groasis sheets describe a siphon in Growboxx and a capped cover opening in Waterboxx. These features establish that additional filling is contemplated, but give no tested autonomous aircraft connection, opening diameter, docking tolerance, automatic cap handling or spill-control protocol. An aerial refill concept therefore needs an independently demonstrated transfer interface and a site/plant-specific refill requirement. Existing citrus-drone evidence concerns canopy spray deposition and cannot validate reservoir filling. Capacity, refill volume, daily release and litres per plant per event must remain distinct.

topics.label: UAS Open-category conditions (EASA FAQ snapshot)
topics.description: The library copy of EASA FAQ 116450, last updated 1 February 2024, describes Open-category entry conditions involving the applicable class/legacy/private-build route, people separation, visual line of sight, maximum 120 m height, no dangerous goods and no material dropping. It is a short dated FAQ, not the complete aviation rule set, an operational authorization or a current legal check. A drone’s payload or nominal positioning capability alone therefore cannot establish that a proposed water delivery or reservoir-refill operation is permitted. The FAQ’s wording must not be used to decide how a specific transfer operation is legally classified.

findings.label: Reservoir rates and capacity do not supply a species event dose
findings.text: Growboxx lists 100–500 mL/day depending on soil characteristics, with no checked storage capacity in this sheet. Waterboxx lists approximately 15 L content and variable 700–18 mL/day, average 50 mL/day, with a possible two-plant opening. These quantities are product specifications: neither document supplies litres per carob plant per watering event or a demonstrated drone refill schedule. Growboxx lists 550 g and 40 × 40 × 20 cm; Waterboxx approximately 1,400 g and 50 × 22 cm. No aircraft compatibility is inferred from these masses.

browse_groups.description: Compare biodegradable Growboxx, reusable Waterboxx and the separately documented Cocoon. The Groasis documents are supplier sheets, including performance claims and application limits; they do not establish an autonomous drone-refill system. Open refill access to inspect that unresolved integration requirement.
